messages.subject: Calculating thetas
parts:
Phil,


I've been struggling to understand some results of the parameter estimation.
I've used two mirt.model:

m3pl2 <- mirt.model("F1 = 1-45 
                   PRIOR = (1-45, a1, lnorm, 0.2, 0.2), 
                   (1-45, d, norm, 0, 1), 
                   (1-45, g, norm, 0, 0.2)
                   MEAN = F1")

m3pl <- mirt.model("F1 = 1-45 
                   PRIOR = (1-45, a1, lnorm, 1, 0.3), 
                   (1-45, d, norm, 0, 1), 
                   (1-45, g, norm, -1.386294, .2)")

When I free the estimation, I get much more coherents parameters, here is the csv with the parameters calculated freely, as Parameters1.csv
The parameters I get using the second mirt.model is Parameters2.csv

Since I've been working with a test that is used to measure if the Student had or not concluded High School and as a way to ingress on Universities, the parameters I get using the freely estimation seen way more coherent.
Said that the official results is given on a 0-5 theta range, with some of the thetas between 4-5, by some I mean a good number.
However, when I calculate the fscores with that parameters I don't get thetas higher than 4.
Is there any way to get to that result, with some thetas between 4-5, using some function or some feature of fscores?


Thanks.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Calculating thetas
parts:
For model 1, is the model identified if you free the latent mean? I don't think that it is. Also, in both models, are you aware that mirt applies an internal logit transformation for the g parameters during estimation? Hence, putting a normal prior with a mean at 0 is really centring the prior around 0.5, which is pretty high. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mixedmirt and estimation using EM Algorithm
parts:
mixedmirt() currently only supports the MH-RM algorithm. Latent regression models can be run through mirt() though, but it sounds like you have an additional random effect structure to account for, so that likely is not applicable. 

Regarding invariance tests, there are different styles of this but multipleGroup() is currently only for comparisons between two groups at a time, while mixedmirt() is more about conditional regression type models (where certain types of uniform DIF are possible, but the full-blown DIF approaches in IRT are generally not supported). 

On Wed, Dec 19, 2018 at 8:37 PM Jayashri Srinivasan <jaya...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Phil,

I have been using mirt() and multiple Group() to carry out some analysis that I am working on and since the items are on Likert-scale I am using GRM. My full model will include a 3-level model with the GRM model at level-1 to model the item responses and level-2 and 3 are the student and school levels, respectively. For this analysis I am hoping to use mixedmirt (). 

My question is does mixedmirt() employ EM algorithm (is it possible) or does it only use MH-RM for estimation. I read the documentation and it seems that the only option is MH-RM, but I wanted to check.  

Also, I am wondering when I test for invariance I know multipleGroup() is using a graded model, but do you have any pointers on assessing invariance using mirt or mixedmirt  and multiple group for my 3-level model.  

Thank you 
Jayashri
